newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share market rises 1.0 pct to new closing peak.
newsitem.headline: NZ share market rises 1.0 pct to new closing peak.

text.p: * NZ share prices end one percent higher at new record
* Top 40 Index peaks at 2,521.60. Telecom main driver
* Market thumbs its nose at sharp sell-off in rates
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +26.53 at 2,519.68
373 +1 * NZSC cap index +11.71 at 5,244.31
351 -1 * NZMC .NZMC cap index +10.31 at 1,982.57

772 +18 * Other movers - +30 +11
The New Zealand share market thumbed its nose at a major sell-off in debt markets to close at another record high on Thursday.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed at 2,519.68, up 26.53 points (1.06 percent), slightly off its 2,519.68 intraday peak.
The index is now at its highest point since its inception in 1991. Compared to its predecessor, the Barclays Index, the market also is at a fresh high since the 1987 crash.
Brokers were stunned by the robustness of the rally after Reserve Bank governor Don Brash fired a warning shot across the bows of the money markets.
Brash said monetary conditions had eased too far, which prompted a massive selloff in bills and bonds.
September bank bill futures were 17 basis points weaker at 92.86 on turnover of more than 10,000 lots.
Telecom was the main driver for the share market, climbing 18 cents to NZ$7.72, but Lion Nathan was also strong, ending five cents up at five at $3.80.
"I was surprised by the robustness of the market in the face of extreme weakness in the bonds," Murray Rutherford at SBC Warburg said.
"You would have to say that today's rise is surprising and may be difficult to sustain," he said.
Rutherford said there was also the likelihood of some weak corporate earnings reports in the short term.
Telecom's rise was more a function of liquidity, now that two tranches of the share buyback are now complete, he said.
"It's been driven more by supply and demand than by fundamentals," he said, adding the stock was now reaching the upper end of SBC's valuation.
-- James Gray, Auckland newsroom +64 9 302 1253
